justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Broaden the R6 base value set to include the R4 Basic Resource Types codes while recommending version-independent resource-type codings.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve many R4 codings, but creates durable duplicate code representations and validation ambiguity for a modifier element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of aligning `Basic.code` with current and historical FHIR resource type identifiers is reasonable because `Basic.code` is a modifier that controls interpretation of the resource. A less-breaking base design was possible, but it would keep legacy lower-case Basic Resource Types beside official resource-type codes and weaken the terminology cleanup. Given the uneven overlap and modifier semantics, the breakage is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternative would have been to compose the R6 extensible value set from both version-independent resource types and the old R4 Basic Resource Types system, or to retain a weaker base binding while making resource-type codes preferred in guidance. That would preserve old instances with only the old coding. It is only a partial alternative: old abbreviated codes and official resource-type names would both remain valid for the same concept, deprecated representations might never disappear, and validators/consumers would face ambiguity on an element that determines the whole Basic instance meaning. A ConceptMap or dual-coding migration note would help migration but is not itself a backwards-compatible base design.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 base-design break: R4 date values remain valid at date precision for R6 dateTime.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is only for R6-to-R4 downgrade; preserving full timestamps in R4 would require truncation or an extension/backport mitigation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing dateTime precision directly supports the existing ordering and audit-like requirement and does not invalidate R4 date-only instances in R6. The only material incompatibility is reverse conversion when R6 uses time-of-day precision, so the change is probably justified under the calibration rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the R6 type widening preserves R4 instances. Keeping `created` as `date` and adding an extension for time precision would be an R6-to-R4 downgrade-friendly design, but that is a mitigation/backport strategy rather than a less-breaking answer to an R4-to-R6 base-design break.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 base-design break: R6 adds Device and CareTeam targets while preserving every R4 author target.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: There is no R4-to-R6 compatibility tradeoff; R6-to-R4 downgrade of new targets needs mapping, rejection, Provenance, or extension handling.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting device-generated and team-authored Basic resources fits the existing authorship definition and preserves all R4-valid author references. The incompatibility arises only when converting newer R6 content with Device or CareTeam authors back to R4, so the base R6 widening is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because all R4 target profiles remain valid. Keeping the R4 target list and representing Device or CareTeam authorship through Provenance, extensions, or profile-specific rules would be a downgrade-friendly mitigation, not a less-breaking base-design alternative for existing R4 instances.
